newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China army unit enters HK to prepare for takeover.
newsitem.headline: China army unit enters HK to prepare for takeover.

text.p: China's army made an historic move into Hong Kong on Monday, driving through the border post from Shenzhen to mark the beginning of the end for Britain's 150 years of rule in the crown colony.
A 40-strong advance contingent from the People's Liberation Army (PLA) arrived to prepare garrison facilities for China's July 1 takeover of the territory.
The soldiers wore full uniform but carried no weapons as they drove through the Lok Ma Chau land land crossing into the British colony in eight staff vehicles from China's booming Shenzhen region.
After going through immigration and customs procedures at the crossing, they headed for the Prince of Wales Barracks of the British armed forces in central Hong Kong.

Major-General Zhou Borong, who will be second-in-command of the future Chinese garrison, stepped from his black Audi car on to Hong Kong soil where he was saluted by senior Chinese diplomat Chen Zuo'er and other Chinese and Hong Kong officials. He also shook hands with British liaison officers.
British soldiers clambered aboard the vehicles, already registered and fitted with Hong Kong number plates, to help guide the PLA men across 30 km (20 miles) of Hong Kong territory to the barracks.

Britain hands its last Asian colony back to China at midnight on June 30 under a 1984 treaty which promises the bustling territory of 6.4 million people a further 50 years of freewheeling capitalism and quasi autonomy.
The convoy was made up of black Audis, white vans, a cross-country Mitsubishi Pajero and camouflaged army trucks, believed to be carrying the PLA's communications equipment.
Travelling with the general were 22 field officers, eight junior officers and nine soldiers.
Hong Kong laid on substantial security, with most roads near the frontier post closed to traffic for the crossing, reporters at the scene said. Paramilitary police in colonial uniform stood guard.

From the Chinese side of the border, the official Xinhua news agency reported that the PLA men received a solemn send-off by future garrison commander Major-General Liu Zhenwu and political commissar Major-General Xiong Ziren.
A PLA band bade farewell to the men with a rendering of the "March of the PLA".

In his speech General Liu called on the advance party to "carry forward the fine tradition of the PLA and conscientiously perform their sacred duties in strict accordance with the Garrison Law... and Hong Kong laws, to convey a good image of the PLA as 'ethical troops' by their concrete actions".

Chen Xiangwen, a staff officer of the PLA Hong Kong troops, said on behalf of the advance party that they were determined to win honour for both their country, the PLA and the ruling Chinese Communist Party.
They were the first of up to 10,000 PLA troops due to form the Hong Kong garrison after Britain hands back its bustling capitalist outpost to Communist-ruled China.
Up to 200 advance troops are to be phased in before handover day. By then Britain will have moved out most of its garrison, which once numbered up to 10,000.
The last of the Black Watch regiment are due to fly out just after the midnight June 30 flag change.
The advance PLA contingent was the first military presence China has been allowed in the run-up to the takeover.

The prospect of the PLA's arrival worried many Hong Kong people who remember that its tanks charged into Beijing's Tiananmen Square in 1989 and crushed the student-led democracy movement there, leaving hundreds, possibly thousands dead.

China has been at pains in recent months to soothe those anxieties with a PLA charm offensive at an interim base over the border in Shenzhen, parading the elite troops chosen for Hong Kong garrison duty and extolling their virtue, discipline and high education level.
